capabilities.title: Typed, validated catalogs and English interface catalog
capabilities.contract: English is the only complete installed catalog. Application copy, including Electron-native dialogs, skill-specific Assistant completion labels, and fallback Proposal summaries, is catalog-validated; production surfaces use the selected Interface locale, localized text is excluded from selectors and logic, and generated supporting UI text requests the active Interface locale independently of Article language.
capabilities.persistence: Localized defaults become Article data only when author-editable content is created.

capabilities.title: Semantic controls, focus treatment, keyboard navigation, and non-color cues
capabilities.contract: Workspace and Settings controls expose semantic labels, keyboard access, visible focus, and non-color status conventions, including labelled proposal decisions and patterned diffs. Tab and Shift+Tab move through visible Workspace focus areas in the documented order, preferring each area’s stable entry target; Settings has separate navigation and content areas. Settings content and compact navigation retain native Tab traversal between controls, switching areas at their boundaries; desktop navigation uses Up, Down, Home, and End between its back action and section buttons, activated with Enter or Space. Assistant chat keeps Up and Down for scrolling and uses Left and Right for actionable results. Article Header and Status use Left and Right between controls, while Library uses Up and Down outside its search field. Dialogs, menus, toolbars, tab lists, and text editors retain their established keyboard behavior.
capabilities.persistence: Accessibility behavior is derived from rendered controls and does not persist sensitive state.

capabilities.title: Shortcut hints, normalization, conflict detection, and command registration
capabilities.contract: Key bindings normalize, resolve defaults, identify conflicts, and register commands.
capabilities.persistence: Author-selected overrides persist in Application Settings.
limitations: Complete workspace-action wiring remains follow-up work.

capabilities.title: Shared success and error provider with viewport
capabilities.contract: Recoverable failures are presented through a shared notification API with localized action-specific recovery guidance, without exposing sensitive values or repeating an identical active error notification.

capabilities.title: Shared contracts, HTTP constants, and transport-boundary validation
capabilities.contract: Shared validation and transport constants reject malformed data before it reaches application behavior, including bounded Proposal-change summary inputs; application-owned conflicts are mapped at each transport boundary, and provider-specific prompt roles are normalized at the provider boundary. Electron IPC uses a typed allowlist and renderer-safe error payloads.
capabilities.persistence: Invalid provider or transport payloads are not persisted as valid application data.

capabilities.title: Server-side secrets, local materials, minimal context, redacted diagnostics, and storage opt-in
capabilities.contract: Secrets remain server-side, including custom-named values loaded from the project .env file before local-service startup; materials remain local, only necessary request context is sent, and supporting Proposal summaries explicitly disable provider-side response storage. The local service emits redacted JSON Lines diagnostics for startup, recoverable request failures, and backup failures without exposing Article or model bodies. On POSIX, the Skladno data directory and SQLite files are owner-only; Windows ACLs and browser-selected backup folders remain platform-controlled. Editorial adapters also emit allowlisted stage names, timings, finish reasons, failure categories, and HTTP failure status without raw SDK error logging.
capabilities.persistence: Private content is not logged or traced by default; diagnostics write to process stdout or stderr without a log file. Provider-side response storage is disabled unless enabled. POSIX local databases are restricted to the current user.

capabilities.title: SQLite persistence and Article schema migrations
capabilities.contract: Startup applies forward-only Article schema migrations without deleting the database; persistence composition uses focused repositories directly. Pre-Article prototype databases are unsupported and are no longer detected or automatically deleted.
capabilities.persistence: SQLite remains the durable local data store after migration.

capabilities.title: Local Article conversation records
capabilities.contract: Greetings, messages, request scope, completions, and safe failure or cancellation status are isolated per Article; completed Proposal content, localized change summaries, and accepted Revision links remain locally recoverable with their base Revision, and author messages retain resolved skills and offsets. Failed and cancelled retries reconstruct author content, skill, scope, and translation target solely from the local original request.
capabilities.persistence: Conversation records and immutable Revision links are local and cascade with their Article; fixed application messages use stable templates while author and model content remain authored text.

capabilities.title: Persistent application-level checkpoint, Revision, backup, and future sync activity
capabilities.contract: A future activity center is distinct from popup-notification history and does not replace contextual recovery.
capabilities.persistence: Deferred until the post-MVP design and storage contract are approved.

capabilities.title: Accounts, sync, teams, analytics, direct publishing, imports, exports, and remaining alternate clients
capabilities.contract: These capabilities remain outside the validated MVP editorial loop. The Windows Electron updater is tracked as an implemented Application capability and Debian desktop support is tracked as a partial Application capability pending installed acceptance evidence; signed releases remain deferred to #168, and macOS, mobile, and browser-offline clients remain separate work.
capabilities.persistence: No persistence or network surface is introduced for deferred MVP work.

scenarios.title: Installed interface catalogs must be complete
preconditions: A locale catalog is registered for the application.
expected: The complete English catalog validates and is the only installed catalog.

scenarios.title: Electron native dialogs use the interface locale catalog
preconditions: The Electron main process needs to show a startup, shutdown, or Draft-checkpoint dialog.
scenarios.event: The native dialog options are created.
expected: Titles, messages, details, and buttons come from the catalog for the selected Interface locale.
forbidden: User-visible English literals in the Electron main process.

scenarios.title: Workspace layout controls remain accessible
scenarios.event: The author navigates or resizes workspace panels.
expected: Panel controls expose accessible labels and semantic separators.
forbidden: Panel behavior conveyed by color alone.

scenarios.title: Key bindings normalize and detect conflicts
preconditions: Default bindings and an author override are available.
scenarios.event: The binding resolver normalizes and compares key chords.
expected: Defaults, explicit unassignment, and duplicate chords are resolved deterministically.
forbidden: Silent acceptance of conflicting effective chords.

scenarios.title: Notification errors remain recoverable and redacted
preconditions: An application client error or unknown exception occurs.
scenarios.event: The notification provider presents the failure.
expected: A useful localized failure notification names the failed action or condition and a safe next step.
Repeated reports of the same active failure produce one notification.
forbidden: Private diagnostic detail displayed to the author.
Implementation, transport, provider, credential, or Article-body details displayed to the author.

scenarios.title: Malformed health transport data is rejected
preconditions: A health response is received from the local service.
scenarios.event: The shared contract validates the response.
expected: Valid health data is accepted and malformed data is rejected.
forbidden: Malformed transport data becomes application state.

scenarios.title: Provider response storage remains opt-in
preconditions: Server configuration is loaded with or without storage settings.
scenarios.event: The configuration parser resolves privacy settings.
expected: Provider response storage is disabled by default.
forbidden: An ambiguous storage value enables provider response storage.

scenarios.title: Local diagnostics redact private data
preconditions: The local service has environment-variable values and private Article or model content.
scenarios.event: The service records startup, recoverable request, or backup diagnostics.
expected: Structured local events include stable event context and safe error metadata.
forbidden: Diagnostics containing API keys, environment-variable values, full Article or model bodies, raw error messages, or stacks.
A diagnostics write failure interrupts the local service.

scenarios.title: Startup preserves the Article database
preconditions: An Article database contains persisted author data.
scenarios.event: The database is closed and reopened.
expected: Persisted Article data remains available after startup.

scenarios.title: Assistant conversation records remain isolated per Article
preconditions: An Article has an Assistant greeting and author request.
expected: Greeting templates and resolved author skill metadata remain available for the Article.

scenarios.title: Data-protection activity center is explicitly deferred
scenarios.event: A change proposes persistent activity-center work.
expected: The work is tracked as post-MVP rather than inferred into current scope.
forbidden: Treating popup notification history as the activity center.

scenarios.title: Deferred MVP capabilities remain out of scope
scenarios.event: An MVP implementation change is planned.
expected: The capability remains deferred unless the active issue explicitly changes scope.
forbidden: Silent introduction of deferred product surface.
